summary: 26-year-old woman with known asthma: 2 days of worsening wheeze after a cold, unable to complete sentences; RR 28, HR 118, SpO₂ 94 %, PEF 180 L/min (43 % of best). BTS/SIGN acute severe asthma.

inputs.hpi: Known asthma since childhood, one previous admission, no ICU. Two days of a cold, then worsening wheeze and chest tightness; using her salbutamol inhaler every hour without relief. Cannot finish sentences. Attending to book excision of a pilonidal sinus. Best PEF 420 L/min.

exam.general: Sitting forward, using accessory muscles, speaking in phrases.
exam.respiratory: Widespread polyphonic expiratory wheeze, good air entry, RR 28.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute severe asthma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute severe asthma (PEF 43% of best, RR 28, HR 118, cannot complete sentences): oxygen, back-to-back nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, prednisolone, emergency transfer.

mustInclude.note: High-dose inhaled beta2 agonist is first-line.

guideline.name: BTS/SIGN 158 - British guideline on the management of asthma
guideline.section: Section 9 acute asthma in adults: acute severe = PEF 33-50% best/predicted, RR >=25/min, HR >=110/min or inability to complete sentences; life-threatening = PEF <33%, SpO2 <92%, silent chest, cyanosis, poor respiratory effort, arrhythmia, exhaustion, altered consciousness, hypotension; oxygen to SpO2 94-98%, high-dose inhaled beta2 agonist, ipratropium in severe/life-threatening, prednisolone 40-50 mg, IV magnesium sulphate for severe asthma not responding; Section 12 pregnancy: treat as in non-pregnant patients, do not withhold steroids, fetal monitoring in acute severe asthma
guideline.citation: British Thoracic Society / Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. SIGN 158. Edinburgh: SIGN; 2019.

guideline.name: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) - Global strategy for asthma management and prevention
guideline.section: Management of worsening asthma and exacerbations: assess severity; SABA (+ ipratropium in severe), controlled oxygen, systemic corticosteroids; transfer to acute care if features of severe or life-threatening exacerbation
guideline.citation: Global Initiative for Asthma. GINA report 2024. www.ginasthma.org.

guideline.name: BTS guideline for oxygen use in healthcare and emergency settings
guideline.section: Target SpO2 94-98% for most acutely ill patients; 88-92% for patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure (e.g. COPD) pending blood gases
guideline.citation: O'Driscoll BR, Howard LS, Earis J, Mak V. Thorax. 2017;72(Suppl 1):ii1-90.

rationale: Base asthma case: two acute severe features (PEF 33-50%, RR >=25, HR >=110, inability to complete sentences) are present. PANE has no asthma node.
